Thanks for the run-through last week. Attached is a very rough draft of the Partner Center claim flow we discussed (draft_claim_flow_v1.pdf). The ask from MSFT is to lock down a lightweight handoff pattern we can operationalize across seller teams for Contoso and similar mid-market accounts.

Key points I'm hoping we can cover in a short sync:
- How Partner Center referral claim is surfaced to field sellers (email vs. Partner Center inbox)
- Ownership arbitration when accounts overlap (who gets first right-of-way)
- Fallback routing when the mapped seller doesn't respond within SLA

Adding a quick note on the Contoso mapping — pulled from our account fabric:
- Contoso Corp (corp-id: CT-773) — primary owner: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com (EMEA owner)
- Contoso North America (corp-id: CT-773-NA) — primary owner: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com (US west)
- Contoso Cloud Practice (corp-id: CT-773-CP) — no owner assigned (legacy merge)

If Partner Center forwards a referral to "Contoso" without the tenant/segment qualifier, our current ingestion maps it to CT-773 (EMEA) by default. That will create a false-positive claim for EMEA sellers and block US seller outreach.

Proposed short-term fixes:
1) Require "region" on inbound referral payload (small validation change on intake).
2) If region absent, route to a "claim triage" queue owned by field ops for 24 hours before auto-assign.
3) Add a simple owner-override action in the Partner Center UI for sellers to escalate claim ownership.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123 (mapping export + notes)

Quick note on fallback policy: if a mapped seller does not accept a claim within 24 hours we should:
- 1) bump to a regional "seller-on-call" (rotating pager)
- 2) notify the referrer and the CS lead for the account
- 3) if still unclaimed after 72 hours, route to central field ops for assignment

I'll bring the SLA wording and an example notification template to the call.
